rule: With exactly one on-demand import (`import a.b.*`), a simple type name that is not in the file's package, not imported singly and not a java.lang type is `a.b.Name` (medium); with more than one such import it stays unqualified, low. ... Honest low (do not resolve by guessing): ... types reachable only through more than one wildcard import.
source: KNOWN_GAP: types reachable only through several wildcard imports stay medium
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. Two on-demand imports (java.io.*, java.util.*): List, ArrayList and StringWriter are reachable only through them, so the type names stay unqualified and the edges are low, even though a reader can tell which package holds each. String is a java.lang type, excluded from the wildcard rule, so java.lang.String#length stays medium.
